paper_title: Exotic energy injection in the early universe II: CMB spectral distortions and constraints on light dark matter
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, converted from decay lifetime tau via Gamma = g^2 m^3/(64 pi)
notes: Paper extends Planck CMB anisotropy constraints on DM->gamma gamma decay down to m_chi = 2R ~ 27.2 eV (tau > ~1e25 s), and recasts them as limits on the ALP-photon coupling g_agamma (Fig. 10, spanning ~10 eV to ~1 MeV). No numerical table of g_agamma is provided; I converted the stated lifetime limits (tau >~ 1e25 s at m=2R from text; tau values at 10 keV, 85 keV, 720 keV from the chi->gamma gamma legend in Figs. 2/7/9, which lie on the CMB anisotropy exclusion boundary from Ref. [9] that the new work reproduces/extends) using Gamma = g^2 m^3/(64 pi) with hbar = 6.582e-25 GeV s. Intermediate points between 27 eV and 10 keV (the genuinely new region) are shown only graphically in Figs. 9-10, so coverage is sparse. This is a cosmological (CMB) bound assuming ALPs are all of DM, but no local DM density is relevant. Confidence level not explicitly stated; Planck-based limits in Ref. [9] are 95% CL.
